mn11:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthi in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapindika’s Park.
mn11:1.3: There he addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn11:2.1: ‘Bhikkhus, only here is there a monk, only here a second monk, only here a third monk, only here a fourth monk.
mn11:2.2: The doctrines of others are devoid of monks:
mn11:2.3: that is how you should rightly roar your lion’s roar.
mn11:3.1: ‘It is possible that wanderers of other sects here might ask:
mn11:3.2: “But what is the venerable ones’ (source of) comfort and strength that you venerable ones say thus?”
mn11:3.5: Wanderers of other sects who ask thus may be answered in this way:
mn11:3.6: “Friends, four dhammas have been declared to us by the Blessed One who knows and sees, Arahant and Fully Enlightened, on seeing which in ourselves we say thus:
mn11:3.7: ‘Only here is there a monk, only here a second monk, only here a third monk, only here a fourth monk.
mn11:3.8: The doctrines of others are devoid of monks.’
mn11:3.10: We have confidence in the Master, we have confidence in the Dhamma, we have perfected the virtues,
mn11:3.11: and those who share the Dhamma are dear to us
mn11:3.12: whether they are laymen or gone forth and they are loved by us.
mn11:3.13: These are the four dhammas declared by the Blessed One who knows and sees, an Arahant and Fully Enlightened, on seeing which in ourselves we say as we do.”
mn11:4.1: ‘It is possible that wanderers of other sects might say thus:
mn11:4.2: “Friends, we too have confidence in the Master, that is, our Master; we too have confidence in the Dhamma, that is, our Dhamma; we too have perfected the virtues, that is, our virtues;
mn11:4.3: and those who share Dhamma are dear to us too
mn11:4.4: whether they are laymen or gone forth and they are loved by us.
mn11:4.5: what is the distinction here, friends, what is the variance, what is the difference, between you and us?’’
mn11:5.1: Wanderers of other sects who ask thus may be answered in this way:
mn11:5.2: “How then, friends, is the goal? One or many?’’
mn11:5.3: Answering rightly, the wanderers of other sects would answer thus:
mn11:5.4: “Friends, the goal is one, not many.”-
mn11:5.5: ”But, friends, is that goal for one affected by lust or free from lust?’’
mn11:5.6: Answering rightly, the wanderers from other sects would answer thus:
mn11:5.7: “Friends, the goal is for one free from lust, not affected by lust.”-
mn11:5.8: ”But, friends is that goal for one affected by hate or free from hate?’’
mn11:5.10: “Friends, the goal is for one free from hate, not affected by hate.”-
mn11:5.11: ”But, friends, is that goal for one affected by delusion or free from delusion?’’
mn11:5.13: “Friends, the goal is for one free from delusion, not affected by delusion.”-
mn11:5.14: ”But, friends, is that goal for one affected by craving or free from craving?’’
mn11:5.16: “Friends, the goal is for one free from craving, not affected by craving.”-
mn11:5.17: ”But, friends, is that goal for one affected by clinging, or free from clinging?’’
mn11:5.19: “Friends, the goal is for one free from clinging, not affected by clinging.”-
mn11:5.20: ”But, friends, is that goal for one who has vision or for one without vision?’’
mn11:5.22: “Friends, that goal is for one with vision, not for one without vision.”-
mn11:5.23: ”But, friends, is that goal for one who favours and opposes, or for one who does not favour and oppose?’’
mn11:5.25: “Friends, the goal is for one who does not favour and oppose, not for one who favours and opposes.”-
mn11:5.26: ”But, friend, is that goal for one who delights in diversification or for one who has no delight in diversification?’’
mn11:5.28: “Friends, the goal is for one who has no delight in diversification, not for one who delights in diversification.”
mn11:6.1: ‘Bhikkhus, there are these two kinds of views:
mn11:6.2: the view of being and the view of non-being.
mn11:6.3: Any monks or divines who rely on the view of being, adopt the view of being and accept the view of being, are opposed to the view of non-being.
mn11:6.4: Any monks or divines who rely on the view of non-being, adopt the view of non-being and accept the view of non-being, are opposed to the view of being.
mn11:7.1: Any monks or divines who do not understand as they actually are the origin and the disappearance and the gratification and the danger and the escape in (the case of) these two kinds of views, are affected by lust, affected by hate, affected by delusion, affected by craving, affected by clinging, without vision, given over to favouring and opposing, and who delight in diversification, enjoy diversification;
mn11:7.2: they are not liberated from birth, ageing and death, from sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair,
mn11:7.3: they are not liberated from suffering, I say.
mn11:8.1: Any monks or divines who understand as they actually are the origin and the disappearance, and the gratification and the danger and the escape in (the case of) these two kinds of views, are without lust, without hate, without delusion, without craving, without clinging, with vision, not given over to favouring and opposing, and who have no delight in diversification, no enjoyment in diversification;
mn11:8.2: they are liberated from birth, ageing and death, from sorrow and lamentation, pain, grief and despair,
mn11:8.3: they are liberated from suffering, I say.
mn11:9.1: Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds clinging:
mn11:9.3: clinging to sensual desires, clinging to wrong views, clinging to rites and rituals and clinging to a self-doctrine.
mn11:10.1: When certain monks and divines claim to propound the full knowledge of all kinds of clinging,
mn11:10.2: they do not completely describe full knowledge of all kinds of clinging.
mn11:10.3: They describe full knowledge of clinging to sensual desires without describing clinging to (wrong) views, clinging to rites and rituals, or clinging to a self-doctrine.
mn11:10.5: Those good monks and divines do not understand these three instances (of clinging) as they actually are.
mn11:10.6: Consequently while these good monks and divines claim to propound full knowledge of all kinds of clinging,
mn11:10.8: they describe (only) full knowledge of clinging to sensual desires without describing clinging to views, clinging to rites and rituals and clinging to a self-doctrine.
mn11:11.1: When certain monks and divines claim to propound the full knowledge of all kinds of clinging,
mn11:11.3: they describe full knowledge of clinging to sensual desires and clinging to views, without describing clinging to rites and rituals and clinging to a self-doctrine
mn11:11.5: … they do not understand two instances …
mn11:11.8: They describe full knowledge of clinging to sensual desires and clinging to views, without describing clinging to rites and rituals and clinging to a self-doctrine.
mn11:12.1: When certain monks and divines claim to propound the full knowledge of all kinds of clinging,
mn11:12.3: they describe full knowledge of clinging to sensual desires, clinging to views and clinging to rites and rituals, without describing clinging to a self-doctrine
mn11:12.5: they do not understand one instance
mn11:12.8: They describe full knowledge of clinging to sensual desires and clinging to views and clinging to rites and rituals without describing clinging to a self-doctrine.
mn11:13.1: ‘Bhikkhus, in such a Dhamma and Discipline as that it is plain that confidence in the Master is not rightly directed,
mn11:13.2: it is plain that confidence in the Dhamma is not rightly directed,
mn11:13.3: that perfecting of the virtues is not rightly directed,
mn11:13.4: and that the dearness and love among those who share the Dhamma are not rightly directed.
mn11:13.6: Because that is how it is when the Dhamma and the Discipline is ill-expounded, ill-proclaimed, leading nowhere, unconducive to peace and proclaimed by one not fully enlightened.
mn11:14.1: ‘Bhikkhus, when a Tathāgata, an Arahant and Fully Enlightened One, claims to propound full knowledge of all kinds of clinging, he completely describes all kinds of clinging:
mn11:14.2: he describes full knowledge of clinging to sensual desires and clinging to (wrong) view and clinging to rites and rituals and clinging to a self-doctrine.
mn11:15.1: ‘Bhikkhus, in such a Dhamma and Discipline as that it is plain that confidence in the Master is rightly directed,
mn11:15.2: that confidence in the Dhamma is rightly directed,
mn11:15.3: that perfecting of virtues is rightly directed,
mn11:15.4: and that dearness and love among those who share the Dhamma are rightly directed.
mn11:15.6: Because that is how it is when the Dhamma and the Discipline is well-expounded, well-proclaimed, leading onward, conducive to peace, and proclaimed by one fully enlightened.
mn11:16.1: ‘Now these four kind of clinging have what as their source, what as their origin, from what are they born, by what are they produced?
mn11:16.2: ‘These four kinds of clinging have craving as their source, craving as their origin, they are born from craving, and produced by craving.
mn11:16.4: ‘Craving has feeling as its source... produced by feeling.
mn11:16.6: ‘Feeling has contact as its source... produced by contact.
mn11:16.8: ‘Contact has the sixfold base as its source... produced by the sixfold base.
mn11:16.9: ‘The sixfold base has what as its source...?
mn11:16.10: ‘The sixfold base has name-and-form as its source... produced by name-and-form.
mn11:16.12: ‘Name-and-form has consciousness as its source... produced by consciousness.
mn11:16.14: ‘Consciousness has formations as its source... produced by formations.
mn11:16.16: ‘Formations have ignorance as their source, ignorance as their origin, they are born from ignorance, and produced by ignorance.
mn11:17.1: ‘Bhikkhus, as soon as ignorance is abandoned and true knowledge has arisen in a bhikkhu, then with the fading of ignorance and the arising of true knowledge he no longer clings to sensual desires (as fuel for) clinging, or to (wrong) views (as fuel for) clinging, or to rites and rituals (as fuel for) clinging, or to a self-doctrine (as fuel for) clinging.
mn11:17.2: When he does not cling, he has no anguish. When he has no anguish, he attains Nibbāna for himself:
mn11:17.3: Birth is is exhausted, the life divine has been lived out, what can be done is done, there is no more of this in the beyond.’
mn11:17.4: That is what the Blessed One said.
mn11:17.5: The bhikkhus were satisfied, and they delighted in the Blessed One’s words.
